title: fix: keep queued Mooncake linker loads after abort
body:
## Summary

- Stop canceling queued Mooncake direct-linker loads after the unified cache wrapper has already published the restored tree node.
- Keep the pending Mooncake load so the normal layer-wise load path can fill the device slots and release the wrapper lock.
- Match the existing UMBP direct-linker behavior for this abort window.

## Why

`UnifiedCacheLinkerWrapper.load_back()` inserts/publishes the restored prefix into the tree before it queues the backend load. If the request aborts in that window, `release_request()` calls `cache_linker.cancel_queued_load(rid)`.

Mooncake previously popped the pending backend transfer and returned `True`, so the wrapper also dropped its pending load entry and released the lock. The published tree node can then remain visible as a device-cache hit even though its device slots were never populated by Mooncake.

## Reproduction

I set up an H200 rx devbox with Mooncake using `MooncakeTestServices`; RDMA initialization succeeded on `mlx5_0` and the Mooncake metadata/master/store services started successfully.

I also tried to run a service-level E2E with the external linker enabled:

- `Qwen3-4B` could not exercise this path because plain KV uses `_PlainKvStrategy`, which rejects the direct external linker.
- `AgainstEntropy/GLM-5.2-FP8-2L` is a DSA model and matches the supported direct-linker strategy, but the devbox cache only had config/index files, not weights; trying the HF model id also failed with repository 404.

The deterministic state-machine repro below uses the real `UnifiedCacheLinkerWrapper.release_request()` and `MooncakeDirectLinker.cancel_queued_load()` on the same devbox. It models the exact post-publish/pre-layer-load state: wrapper pending exists and Mooncake backend pending exists for the same request.

Before this fix:

```text
before wrapper_pending ['rid-1']
before backend_pending ['rid-1']
before dec_lock_calls []
after wrapper_pending []
after backend_pending []
after dec_lock_calls [(123, 'lock-token')]
```

After this fix:

```text
before wrapper_pending ['rid-1']
before backend_pending ['rid-1']
before dec_lock_calls []
after wrapper_pending ['rid-1']
after backend_pending ['rid-1']
after dec_lock_calls []
```

This confirms the unsafe state transition: the old Mooncake path drops the queued transfer after the tree node has already become visible. The patch keeps the transfer pending so the existing completion path can populate the slots and release the lock.

## Testing

- `python3 -m py_compile python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_direct_linker.py`
- `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_direct_linker.py`
